harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built an Ansible playbook (run from node2, the only node with ansible installed) that creates an SSH host certificate authority on node1 (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca), signs node1's ed25519 host public key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1,10.100.12.10, configures sshd to present that certificate via HostCertificate/HostKey directives, validates config, and restarts sshd. A bootstrap step (ssh-keygen -A + starting the inactive ssh.service, which had no host keys at all on this baseline image) was needed before Ansible/SSH could reach node1 at all. Verified end-to-end: on node2 (the client), removed any pinned host-key known_hosts entries and added only a `@cert-authority node1,10.100.12.10 <CA-pubkey>` trust line, then connected with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes and confirmed via verbose SSH output that the client validated node1 purely via the CA certificate ("Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate"), with no pinned key needed. Then ran the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot-id + service/config baselines on both nodes, restarted node1 (boot_id bdd5de93→b878380d) and confirmed sshd, CA files, and cert-based trust all survived; restarted node2 (boot_id eefaca89→f6406f97) and confirmed the Ansible artifacts, SSH client keys, and CA-trusted connection to node1 still worked afterward.
actions_performed: Diagnosed node1 sshd inactive due to missing host keys (start-limit-hit); ran ssh-keygen -A and enabled/started ssh.service
Provisioned CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY into node1 root authorized_keys and CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY into node2 for passwordless SSH
Set up Ansible inventory/config on node2 (control node) targeting node1

Wrote and ran an Ansible playbook (/root/ansible/ssh-host-cert/site.yml on node2) that creates a CA keypair, signs node1's host key into a host certificate, configures sshd HostCertificate/HostKey, validates, restarts sshd, and fetches the CA pubkey to the control node

Configured node2 as an SSH client trusting node1 solely via a @cert-authority known_hosts line (after removing any pinned host key entries), and verified StrictHostKeyChecking=yes succeeds via the certificate, not key pinning
Captured pre-restart baselines (boot_id, sshd state, CA/cert files, sshd -t) on node1 and node2
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and full recovery of sshd/CA/cert and CA-trust login from node2
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and that Ansible artifacts, SSH keys, and CA-trusted connection to node1 still function

evidence.requirement: Create SSH CA on node1 and have host present a CA-signed certificate, implemented via Ansible
evidence.summary: Ansible inventory/playbook created on node2 (control node); playbook run generated /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca CA keypair on node1, signed the host's ed25519 key into ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub, configured sshd HostCertificate/HostKey, validated config, and restarted sshd successfully (ok=14 changed=7 failed=0).

evidence.requirement: Client connects trusting the CA, without pinning the host key
evidence.summary: Removed pinned host-key entries for node1/10.100.12.10 from node2's known_hosts, added only a @cert-authority line with the CA public key, then connected with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes; verbose SSH log shows 'Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate' and successful authentication, proving cert-based trust rather than key pinning.

evidence.requirement: Bootstrap fix enabling SSH/Ansible connectivity to node1 (host keys were entirely missing, sshd failed to start)
evidence.summary: journalctl showed sshd exiting with 'no hostkeys available'; ran ssh-keygen -A and enabled ssh.service, then confirmed key-based SSH from node2 to node1 worked.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bdd5de93-... and healthy sshd/CA/cert captured; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node1 unreachable then reachable again with new boot_id b878380d-...; post-restart sshd active, CA/cert files intact, sshd -t OK, and CA-trusted SSH login from node2 succeeded again.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id eefaca89-... captured; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node2 unreachable then reachable again with new boot_id f6406f97-...; post-restart Ansible artifacts, SSH client key/known_hosts, and CA-trusted connection to node1 confirmed still functional.
